key_insight: A thermodynamically consistent manifold model can unify premixed deflagration and detonation prediction by iteratively matching the flow solver’s local thermodynamic state with the combustion manifold.
engineering_relevance: This improves LES reliability for compressible reacting flows, making the model more useful for high-speed combustion systems such as rotating detonation engines and other supersonic combustors.
method: Manifold-based turbulent combustion model for compressible premixed flames
Iterative coupling to enforce thermodynamic consistency between model and solver
Captures temperature, radicals, and source-term profiles across deflagrative and detonative regimes
evidence_signal: Validated against one-dimensional cases and high-fidelity RDE-like data, where the thermodynamically consistent model outperformed existing approaches across a broad range of compressible flame regimes.
watch_item: The iterative thermodynamic coupling may increase implementation complexity and computational cost in LES workflows.
paper_title: A Thermodynamically Consistent Manifold Model for Premixed Deflagrations & Detonations
